messages.subject_clean: Upload video on facebook, twitter using R programming
messages.body_plain:
You probably don't want to upload a video just yet - Twitter has a new
video capability that's coming soon, although there are mostly rumors
still.

The easy way right now is to just post a link to the video in a tweet.
YouTube links currently play and others may as well. The hard (but
better) way is to apply for the capability of posting video Twitter
Player Cards (https://dev.twitter.com/cards/types/player).

Images are easy - you can add an image to a Twitter Summary Card or
just post one in a tweet.

messages.subject: can't get auto_test to respond
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm trying to get auto_test from the testthat package to work, but it doesn't seem to update when I change the source file. So here's the contents of toy.R:

toy <- function(a,b) {
a+b+1
}

And the contents of test-toy.R

expect_that(toy(2,2), equals(4))

When I do this, everything works as expected...

> source("toy.R")

> test_dir("./")

1

1. Failure(@test-toy.R#1): (unknown) -------------------------------------------

toy(2, 2) not equal to 4

Mean relative difference: 0.25

Now, I do this and get the expected error...

> auto_test(code_path="./", test_path="./")

Error: toy(2, 2) not equal to 4

Mean relative difference: 0.25

But when I go in and change toy.R to:

toy <- function(a,b) {
a+b
}

and save, nothing happens in the terminal.

Am I missing something? My understanding was that it would automatically re-run the tests when I saved toy.R.

Thanks,
Pat

Here's my info...

> sessionInfo()

R version 3.1.1 (2014-07-10)

Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.1.0 (64-bit)

locale:

[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:

[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base

other attached packages:

[1] testthat_0.9.1

messages.subject: Re: can't get auto_test to respond
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pat,

Hmmm, I suspect because I never expected you to put the test and the
code in the same directory. I'd recommending adopting the standard
package layout.

Hadley

messages.subject: S3 methods across two packages - clash where only one packages implementations are visible
messages.subject_clean: S3 methods across two packages - clash where only one packages implementations are visible
messages.body_plain:
I want to define an S3  method "umxSummary" for  classes in two packages: umx and umx.twin

In package umx, I define the umxSummary stub,  a default function, and implement a useful class: umxSummary.MxModel()

#' umxSummary
#' Report the fit of a OpenMx model or specialized model class (such as ACE, CP etc.)
#' @param model The \code{\link{mxModel}} whose fit will be reported
#' @param ... Other parameters to control model summary
#' @export
umxSummary <- function(model, ...){
UseMethod("umxSummary", model)
}

#' @export
umxSummary.default <- function(model, ...){
print("umxSummary is not defined for objects of class:", class(model))
invisible(object)
}

#' @export
umxSummary.MxModel <- function(model, ...){
print("hi there")
}

This works fine with just this package loaded

I also define this class in the other package "umx.twin" (should I define it there again, or be importing something from umx? )

and another S3 handler for ACE models in this twin library

 umxSummary.MxModel.ACE()

Now, whichever package loads first, the subclass handlers from the other package cannot be seen

so if u,x/twin is loaded second,  umxSummary(ACE), instead of calling  umxSummary.MxModel.ACE(),
calls the default class in the other package, which says no function defined for this class.

QUESTION: What's the correct thing to do? Should I be importing the stub or default function from one package into the other or what?

many thanks for your time reading this, tim

messages.body_plain:
I think the best solution (although it's annoying) in this case is to
define a 3rd package that provides the generic. Then both packages
import and re-export the generic - that lets R figure out that it's
the same generic being used in both places.

Hadley
